name: Scholasticism (Anselm, Aquinas)

objectives.text: Explain that Jesus calls his people to love God with their minds as well as their hearts
Identify Anselm and Thomas Aquinas as Christian teachers who lived long ago and wrote about God
Describe how medieval Christians started cathedral schools and universities such as Paris and Oxford to study God's Word and his world
Explain the meaning of Anselm's motto faith seeking understanding and the scriptural idea of knowledge beginning with the fear of the Lord
Compare how students learned in a medieval monastery with how they learned in a medieval university
Demonstrate the scholastic method by working through a theological question with objections, a reply, and answers to the objections
Explain the goal of Scholasticism to organize Christian teaching into an ordered system, using Peter Lombard's Sentences and Aquinas' Summa Theologiae as examples
Summarize Anselm's argument in Cur Deus Homo for why the Savior had to be both truly God and truly man
Summarize Anselm's ontological argument for God's existence from the Proslogion
Explain how the rediscovery of Aristotle's writings in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries shaped scholastic theology
Summarize Aquinas' Five Ways and relate them to what Scripture teaches about God revealed in creation
Distinguish Aquinas' view of what natural reason can know from the Reformed confession that saving knowledge comes only through Scripture
Compare Anselm's satisfaction view of the atonement with the Reformed doctrine of penal substitution
Analyze how Aquinas' use of Aristotelian categories supported the doctrine of transubstantiation and why the Reformed confessions reject it
Evaluate the strengths and dangers of combining Greek philosophy with biblical theology in medieval Scholasticism
Assess how later Reformed theologians both adopted the scholastic method and corrected scholastic doctrine according to Scripture
Construct a reasoned defense of the Christian faith that draws on a classical scholastic argument while grounding it in Scripture

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (loving God with the mind, Anselm's motto, universities, monastery vs university, goal of systematizing, Cur Deus Homo, Aristotle, Five Ways, Greek philosophy synthesis, atonement). Dropped vague filler (smart thinker, observe universities, apply logic to faith, define university, synthesize achievements). Added scholastic method, Peter Lombard, ontological argument, reason vs revelation, transubstantiation critique, Reformed scholasticism, and apologetics. Recast the atonement defense as a comparison with Reformed penal substitution and replaced WCF 8.4 with 8.5, 8.2, and Heidelberg citations that state the doctrines taught.
